title: Supervisory Litigator (I) (Col to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC
raw_text:
14.     MOS 4452, Supervisory Litigator (I) (Col to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. A Supervisory Litigator is a field grade judge advocate
with the demonstrated skill and experience to not only to meet the
requirements of complex and high-profile cases, but also to lead, mentor, and
supervise judge advocates (including litigators and senior litigators)
assigned to special trial, trial, or defense billets at a regional level.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a judge advocate.

            (2) Must be selected by a board established by the SJA to CMC.

        (3) Must possess at least 72 months of cumulative military justice
experience as a special trial counsel, trial counsel, defense counsel,
victims legal counsel, appellate government or defense counsel, military
trial judge, or appellate judge (or corresponding billets within the Office
of Military Commissions); military justice or criminal law instructor at
formal schools; or military justice policy or counsel assistance program
assignments at Headquarters Marine Corps or the Office of the Judge Advocate
General of the Navy. Experience as a state or federal civilian prosecutor or
a state or federal public defender or defense counsel, or in a litigation
fellowship, may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

    c. Requirements. Judge Advocate Division, in conjunction with DC, M&RA
(MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS.

       d.   Duties

            (1) May serve in any other MOS 4402 billet.

        (2) Serve in regional leadership billets requiring skill and
experience in military and criminal law issues, including as regional special
trial, regional trial, or regional defense counsel.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Lawyers 23-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators.
